purpose: What an interactive front end may show, and what it must show, when it displays this repository's answers. The answer OBJECT already exists — tools/dialogue/ask.mjs prints it as JSON — so this contract declares its shape and the rendering obligations that keep a UI from reproducing conflations the repository spent effort forbidding (knowledge/conflations.json).

questionTypes.rule: LINKED, NOT DUPLICATED. A front end must read the question types from there; a copy here would drift, and an undeclared question type is Refused by the contract rather than guessed at.
questionTypes.generator: tools/interaction/generate.mjs (declared policy: stratified corpus sample + fixed diagnostics)

warrant.noEvidence: true only for a declared derivation over an EMPTY evidence set (contract I1)

mustRender: warrant.refs, or the declared noEvidence case
every role, with null rendered as UNEXPRESSED rather than 'unknown', blank or hidden
additionalMatches when > 0 — the passage holds more frames than the one read
mustNotRender: the roles without the warrant (an answer shown as a bare fact)
a null role filled in from context, from the dialogue, or from another passage

mustRender: reason AND missing — contract I2 requires both, so a UI showing only 'no answer' has dropped the contract
mustNotRender: a plausible reading in place of the reason; 'Unknown' is not a failure to be papered over

Refused.note: an undeclared question type is refused, not guessed at

mustRender: that the condition is STORE-WIDE: nothing is licensed while the store does not replay
mustNotRender: other answers presented as if the store were sound

mustRender: BOTH SIDES by name — a local disagreement is not a store-wide inconsistency
mustNotRender: a single side as the conclusion

claimDisplays.rule: Any claim about what the system can do must carry the readiness gate's claimStatus (the five-rung ladder) and supportKind (evidence | proof | verification | measurement), both from tools/knowledge/claim-status.mjs.
claimDisplays.why: PASS alone conflates 'we ran a bounded measurement above a floor' with 'this holds'. The repository prints 'PASS G2 [bounded-verified / evidence]' for exactly this reason.
claimDisplays.coverage: A coverage figure may not appear without its denominator AND the measured ceiling: 22.43% of ALL passages (18,301/81,575), ceiling 0.244, aspirational target 0.5 NOT met, gate floor 0.15 (revised 2026-09-23 — see tools/knowledge/floors.mjs).

consumableArtifacts.note: 77 works; each entry carries licence tags and a file
passages with ids, source pages, revisions, per-work licence; sections carry sourcePage/sourceRevid
append-only; RETRACTED records must not be shown as live
per-gate claimStatus / supportKind / floors — refresh with readiness.mjs --write
answerability per grammar; its denominator goes stale on every corpus rebuild (that happened once)
918 citations with host/quote/status; verify with tools/intertext/verify.mjs
the two ACCEPTED pairs; measuredNotAdmitted candidates are NOT applied

licensing.rule: A front end that republishes corpus TEXT inherits the per-work licence. Read license.pageTemplates from each data/corpus/works/<id>.json; works with no tag fall to the site-wide default.
licensing.measured: 28 of 77 works carry no licence template and therefore fall to CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + ShareAlike). The rest carry public-domain templates (PD-old, 唐朝作品, …).
licensing.whyItMatters: This is the one obligation a public site takes on that a local tool does not, and it is already measured (knowledge/APERTURES.md A6).

nonClaims: A reading is a DECLARED CONVENTION pinned by supervised labels, not a factual claim about the text.
The citations are a measured textual relation, not influence history, and a quotation found is not proof that the host meant that work.
An unexpressed role is not an unknown role: the construction does not state it, and that is what the missing-role contract (tools/grammar/contract.json missingRoleSemantics) governs.
A front end may not present the repository's non-claims as satisfied: see each artifact above for its own.
